title: Bar Model Word Problems
intro: Use bar models to make the relationship between a whole and its parts visible.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Label the whole and both parts with your student. Place the unknown in its box before choosing an operation.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Total?
95

9 + 5 = 14

The whole is fourteen because both parts belong to it.

Total14
?5

14 − 5 = 9

Nine books were there before the new books arrived.

Ask your student

Which two parts must fit together to make the whole?

If your student needs help

If the student puts the total in a part box, compare the labels with the quantities in the story.

Choosing and using the worksheet

These four questions include an unknown total, an unknown starting amount, and an unknown amount used, with numbers within twenty. They use part-whole bars, not comparison bars or multiplication models. The answer key fills the same blank and shows one suitable equation.
